title: Boolean Conditions
concept: Combine multiple comparisons with &&, ||, and ! to create sophisticated conditions.
why: Real decisions involve multiple factors. Boolean logic lets you express 'if A AND B' or 'if C OR D' naturally.
syntax_ref:
if cond1 && cond2 { ... }      // both must be true
if cond1 || cond2 { ... }      // at least one must be true
if !condition { ... }          // condition must be false
if (a && b) || c { ... }       // group with parentheses
tips: Use `&&` when ALL conditions must be true
Use `||` when ANY condition being true is enough
Use `!` to check the opposite: `if !is_full` instead of `if is_full == false`
Extract complex conditions into named variables for readability
common_mistakes: Writing `&` instead of `&&` — single `&` is bitwise AND
Writing `|` instead of `||` — single `|` is bitwise OR
Forgetting parentheses: `a && b || c` is ambiguous without parens
Using `== true` or `== false` when `!` is cleaner
